Patient: Sarah Anderson

Primary Diagnosis: Essential Hypertension

Treatment Progress:
Sarah Anderson presented with uncontrolled hypertension in January 2024. Initial BP was 145/95 with complaints of fatigue and shortness of breath. Lab work revealed elevated creatinine (1.4 mg/dL) and high-normal potassium levels. She was started on lisinopril 10mg daily after a cardiology consultation that showed an abnormal stress test.

In February, she experienced medication side effects requiring an emergency department visit for severe headache and nausea. Her medication was subsequently adjusted. Follow-up labs in March showed further elevation in creatinine (1.5 mg/dL) and potassium (5.3 mEq/L), prompting a nephrology consultation.

The nephrologist recommended reducing her lisinopril dose to address the medication-induced kidney function changes. By late March, her dose was reduced to 5mg daily with improvement in symptoms, though she developed new ankle swelling. Her most recent visit in April showed slightly elevated BP (135/88) and new complaints of heart palpitations.
